diff_profile.surface: add-only test infrastructure (lint + fixtures + coverage-map row + changeset)

phase3_findings.short_summary: scalar-provenance fixture is vacuous (string is iterable)
phase3_findings.summary: The newly-added scalar-'provenance' guard fixture uses the string "not-a-list", which is iterable, so it does not kill the guard it was added to protect: with the record_shape_error provenance-list guard removed, enumerate() still iterates the string's characters and the downstream isinstance(entry, dict) check returns a different exit-2 error, so the rc==2 assertion (BDS_SP_RC) passes with or without the guard. Its inline comment ('never an uncaught TypeError from enumerate()') describes a failure mode a string provably cannot produce. Verified by mutation: guard-removed + string fixture -> rc=2 (test still green); guard-removed + non-iterable int 7 -> uncaught TypeError, rc=1 (test would go red). Fix: change the provenance fixture value from "not-a-list" to a non-iterable scalar (e.g. 7), mirroring the genuinely non-vacuous pending_sweep_baseline fixture (BDS_SPB_RC) at run.sh:54855-54857.
phase3_findings.failure_scenario: A future refactor deletes the `if not isinstance(prov, list): return "frozen.provenance must be a list"` guard (lint.py:147-148). The suite stays GREEN because the scalar-provenance fixture (string) still exits 2 via the row-shape check, so the regression the fixture was added to catch escapes.

phase3_findings.short_summary: audited {audited} of {audited} prints same var twice
phase3_findings.summary: cmd_check prints 'audited N of N files' interpolating the same variable on both sides of 'of', so the framing is tautological and never surfaces skipped-vs-total drift. Advisory; already noted as staying advisory. Behavior unaffected (real-tree assertion parses only the first number).
phase3_findings.failure_scenario: None (cosmetic). A reader may misread the 'of N' as an audited-vs-total comparison that it is not.

phase3_findings.short_summary: docstring/inline comments carry design narrative beyond 3-line cap
phase3_findings.summary: Several accurate comments (docstring concurrent-merge worked example lines 24-29; the 6-line independent-count rationale in scan() lines 202-207) exceed CLAUDE.md §2.3's three-line / no-derivation cap. Trim to the specification statement plus a pointer. Low severity, non-blocking.
phase3_findings.failure_scenario: None (style). Comment verbosity only; all claims are factually accurate against the code.

checklist_summary.note: Diff is add-only test infrastructure; checklist verification focused on the lint's fail-closed shape guards and the fixture non-vacuousness the task charged. Real-tree reconciliation runs clean (audited 1120 of 1120, rc=0). Both scalar guards in the .py are correct (exit 2, specific breadcrumb, no TypeError). One of the two new run.sh fixtures asserting them is vacuous (see Important finding).

report: Iteration 3 convergence re-review of PR #1973 did NOT converge. The just-applied Minor scalar-guard fix is half-correct: the guard code in record_shape_error() correctly fails closed with exit 2 (verified live) for both a scalar frozen.provenance and a scalar pending_sweep_baseline, with no TypeError. However, one of the two new run.sh regression fixtures added to prove it is VACUOUS: the frozen.provenance fixture uses the iterable string "not-a-list" (run.sh:54852), so removing the guard leaves the suite green (mutation-verified). The pending_sweep_baseline fixture (int 7) is genuinely non-vacuous. Remedy is a one-line change: use a non-iterable scalar (e.g. 7) for the provenance fixture. All four Phase 3 agents returned; no other new Critical/Important findings. The 'audited N of N' cosmetic stays advisory as scoped. AC2 remains scope-deferred; the 5 in-scope ACs are otherwise satisfied by add-only mechanism (index-only tree enumeration #711, adversarial six-shape discipline, fail-closed I/O, presence-not-count reconciliation).
